root:
=== TRAINING GROUNDS ===

The camp bustles with activity even in relative peace. Weapons need sharpening, skills need honing, and a man who doesn't practice is a man who dies in his first real battle. You approach the training grounds where your comrades are already at work.

~ trainingComplete = false

What would you like to focus on today?

* [Sword Training] -> sword_training
  The quintessential skill of any man-at-arms. Your sword is your closest friend and most reliable tool.

* [Archery Practice] -> archery_training
  Distance weapons can save your life when the enemy is too close for comfort and too far for your sword.

* [Formation Training] -> formation_training
  Individual skill matters, but battles are won by disciplined units working together.

* [Camp Life Skills] -> camp_training
  War isn't just fighting. Survival often depends on skills that have nothing to do with weapons.

* [Equipment Preparation] -> equipment_training
  Your gear is your life. A well-maintained set of armor and weapons can mean the difference between victory and death.

=== sword_training ===

You enter the sword training area where several men are already practicing against wooden dummies. The sergeant-at-arms nods grimly. 'Remember, lads: in battle, you fight like you train. Half-assed practice gets you killed.'

~ trainingType = "sword"

* [Practice basic cuts and thrusts] ~ strength = strength + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You spend an hour repeating the fundamental movements. Overhand cuts, underhand thrusts, side-to-side slashes. Your muscles burn with the repetitive motion, but the movements become more fluid, more natural. The sergeant nods approval. 'Good. A man who masters the basics lives longer.'
  -> training_complete

* [Spar with a partner] ~ agility = agility + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1 ~ stress = stress + 1
  You face off against Thomas, a veteran of the Scottish campaigns. He's faster than you, more experienced, but you're stronger. The wooden swords clash as you test each other's defenses. You take a few hits, but you land a solid blow to his ribs that makes him grunt. 'Not bad,' he admits. 'Not bad at all.'
  -> training_complete

* [Practice against multiple opponents] ~ wits = wits + 1 ~ experience = experience + 2 ~ stress = stress + 2
  Three men with wooden swords advance on you. This isn't about strength - it's about positioning, about using one opponent to block another, about never letting them surround you. You take some hits, but you manage to 'kill' two of them before the third gets you. The sergeant actually smiles. 'Now that's thinking like a survivor.'
  -> training_complete

* [Focus on defensive techniques] ~ endurance = endurance + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You practice parries, blocks, and evasions. You learn to read your opponent's intentions, to move just enough to avoid a blow while staying in position to counter-attack. Defense may not be glorious, but it keeps you alive. 'A dead man can't fight,' the sergeant reminds everyone.
  -> training_complete

=== archery_training ===

The archery range is busy with longbowmen practicing their craft. As a man-at-arms, you don't need the mastery of a dedicated archer, but basic competence with a bow or crossbow can save your life.

~ trainingType = "archery"

* [Longbow practice] ~ agility = agility + 1 ~ wits = wits + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  The English longbow is a formidable weapon, but it requires tremendous strength and skill. You struggle at first - the draw weight is enormous, the string bites your fingers. But gradually, your arrows start hitting the target, then clustering closer to the center. 'Good enough for battlefield work,' the archery master acknowledges.
  -> training_complete

* [Crossbow training] ~ strength = strength + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  The crossbow is easier to learn but slower to reload. You practice winding the winch, loading the bolt, aiming carefully. Your first few shots go wide, but soon you're consistently hitting the target. 'Less elegant than a longbow,' the instructor notes, 'but deadlier at close range.'
  -> training_complete

* [Moving target practice] ~ agility = agility + 2 ~ experience = experience + 2 ~ stress = stress + 1
  This is the real test - hitting a target that moves, that ducks and weaves. You miss more than you hit at first, but gradually you learn to lead your target, to anticipate movement. When you finally hit a moving target consistently, the other archers nod in respect.
  -> training_complete

* [Speed shooting] ~ wits = wits + 1 ~ endurance = endurance + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  In battle, you often don't have time for careful aiming. You practice nocking, drawing, and shooting quickly, sacrificing accuracy for speed. Your arrows fly wild at first, but soon you're putting them on target faster than most men-at-arms could manage.
  -> training_complete

=== formation_training ===

Individual skill is valuable, but battles are won by units that fight together. Today you're practicing shield wall tactics and battlefield maneuvers.

~ trainingType = "formation"

* [Shield wall practice] ~ endurance = endurance + 2 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You and ten other men form a shield wall, practicing locking shields together, moving as one unit, presenting an unbreakable front to the enemy. It's grueling work - the weight of shields pressing on you, the need to maintain perfect positioning. But when the 'enemy' charges, your wall holds firm.
  -> training_complete

* [Wedge formation drill] ~ charisma = charisma + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You practice the wedge formation - a V-shaped formation designed to break enemy lines. As the point of the wedge, you have to be aggressive but controlled, breaking through while maintaining formation integrity. It requires trust in the men behind you, the ability to lead while following.
  -> training_complete

* [Battlefield communication] ~ wits = wits + 2 ~ experience = experience + 1
  On a noisy battlefield, visual signals and shouted commands are vital. You practice the standard commands, the hand signals, the drum beats that coordinate movement. You learn to give clear commands, to understand signals instantly, to keep your head in chaos.
  -> training_complete

* [Flanking maneuvers] ~ agility = agility + 1 ~ wits = wits + 1 ~ experience = experience + 2
  You practice moving around enemy formations, striking from the sides or rear. It requires timing, coordination, and the ability to read the flow of battle. When your unit successfully executes a complex flanking maneuver against the 'enemy,' even the sergeant looks impressed.
  -> training_complete

=== camp_training ===

War is mostly waiting punctuated by moments of terror. The skills that keep you alive between battles are just as important as combat skills.

~ trainingType = "camp"

* [Field medicine training] ~ wits = wits + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  The camp surgeon teaches you the basics: how to clean wounds, how to stop bleeding, how to set broken bones, how to recognize infection. You practice on dummies, learning to work quickly and precisely. 'A man who can save his comrades is as valuable as one who can kill enemies,' the surgeon tells you.
  -> training_complete

* [Foraging and scavenging] ~ luck = luck + 1 ~ wits = wits + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You learn to identify edible plants, to track small game, to find water sources, to scavenge useful materials from abandoned places. These skills can mean the difference between eating and starving when supply lines fail. You spend hours in the woods, learning nature's secrets.
  -> training_complete

* [Camp security] ~ endurance = endurance + 1 ~ wits = wits + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You practice setting up watches, identifying potential threats, securing the perimeter, responding to night attacks. You learn to move quietly in the dark, to recognize the sounds of danger, to wake instantly and respond effectively.
  -> training_complete

* [Social skills and networking] ~ charisma = charisma + 2 ~ reputation = reputation + 5 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You spend time in the camp tavern, talking with comrades, learning rumors, building alliances. You discover who owes whom favors, who has useful skills, who can be trusted in a fight. In camp society, information and relationships can be as valuable as steel.
  -> training_complete

=== equipment_training ===

Your gear is your life. A well-maintained set of equipment and the knowledge to use it properly can keep you alive when everything else fails.

~ trainingType = "equipment"

* [Armor maintenance] ~ strength = strength + 1 ~ endurance = endurance + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You spend hours cleaning, repairing, and adjusting your armor. You learn to fix leather straps, to patch dents in metal, to ensure every piece fits properly. You practice moving in your armor, fighting in it, living in it. Well-maintained armor can be the difference between a bruise and a mortal wound.
  -> training_complete

* [Weapon care and repair] ~ wits = wits + 1 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You learn to sharpen blades properly, to repair wooden hafts, to maintain the balance of your weapons. A well-cared-for sword can save your life, while a neglected one might break at the critical moment. You practice with whetstones and files, learning the crafts that keep your tools deadly.
  -> training_complete

* [Load bearing and packing] ~ endurance = endurance + 2 ~ experience = experience + 1
  You learn to pack efficiently, to distribute weight properly, to carry everything you need without being overburdened. You practice marching with full pack, fighting with it, living with it. Proper load management can prevent exhaustion that could get you killed.
  -> training_complete

* [Emergency field repairs] ~ luck = luck + 1 ~ wits = wits + 1 ~ experience = experience + 2
  What do you do when your sword breaks in battle? When your armor is damaged? When your equipment fails? You learn improvisational repair techniques using whatever materials are available. You practice quick fixes that might not be pretty but will keep you fighting until proper repairs can be made.
  -> training_complete

=== training_complete ===

~ trainingComplete = true

=== TRAINING COMPLETE ===

{trainingComplete ? Your training session is complete. You feel more confident, more prepared for the challenges ahead. The sweat and effort will pay off when steel meets steel on the battlefield. : You haven't completed any training yet. Choose a discipline to practice.}

Your improved skills:
{trainingComplete ? You've gained valuable experience and improved your abilities. : Continue training to improve your capabilities.}

* [Return to training selection] -> START
  There's always more to learn, more skills to master.

* [Leave the training grounds]
  You've done enough for today. Time to rest or attend to other duties.
  -> END
